svg.title: Japan at a glance — a one-page infographic
svg.desc: An editorial-style static infographic about Japan: a schematic map with the four largest cities, an explanatory text about the archipelago, a full-width paragraph, a bar chart of nominal GDP in current US dollars from 2015 to 2024, a donut chart of population by nationality and a list of what to visit, with legends and a source note.
svg.text: Cities, population and economy — the archipelago in figures

g.text: Four main islands and the country's four largest cities
Schematic map: simplified coastlines, city dots approximate
Japan arcs some 3,000 km off the east coast of
Asia, from subarctic Hokkaido to subtropical
Okinawa. Four main islands — Honshu, Hokkaido,
Kyushu and Shikoku — hold nearly all of the
roughly three-quarters of the land, so cities and
farms crowd onto narrow coastal plains.
Main islands: Honshu · Hokkaido · Kyushu · Shikoku
A constitutional monarchy with an elected parliament, Japan rebuilt itself after 1945 into the world's second-largest
economy, then slid to fourth as growth stalled, the population aged and the yen weakened. It is a country of
high-speed rail and robotics, 26 UNESCO World Heritage sites, quiet shrines — and a shrinking workforce to carry them.
Japan's nominal output is still near where it stood
a quarter-century ago. Through decades of near-
zero inflation, growth averaged barely 1% a year.
In dollar terms the curve now falls: the yen lost
roughly a third of its value against the dollar
between 2021 and 2024, so the same domestic
economy translates into smaller export figures.
Older pressures remain: an ageing society, a
shrinking workforce, debt above 250% of GDP.
2022–24: a weaker yen pulls US$ values down
Sources: Statistics Bureau of Japan; Immigration Services
Agency · 2024 estimates, rounded to one decimal point
Six stops that explain the country
Ideas compiled from Japan National Tourism Organization listings

svg.text: Static SVG infographic · 1200 × 1800 · no live data

g.text: Nominal GDP in current US$ trillions: IMF World Economic Outlook, 2015–2024; the 2024 figure is provisional and may be revised.
Population, land area, coastline and nationality shares: Statistics Bureau of Japan, Immigration Services Agency and Geospatial Information Authority of Japan, 2024 estimates.
Map is a schematic simplification of the archipelago; island outlines and city markers are approximate. Percentages may not total 100 because of rounding.
